reasons: No test or check was found for this data file.
The wording was condensed from a source article that is not included, so it cannot be verified here.

terms.meaning: A simple idea that helps a person think through a problem, such as second-order thinking.
A group of related mental models that share a heading in the brain picture.
A fixed name used to refer to an item in code, which must stay the same once other files use it.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Where the mental models come from
sections.what: Explains what the file is for: short one-line versions of mental models that feed the hero brain picture. Logic families sit on the left side and families about nature, art and people sit on the right side.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code, beyond the header comment describing the source and the left and right split.
sections.watch_out: The header names a source article that is not in the project, so the one-line wording cannot be checked against it.

sections.name: MentalModel
sections.title: One mental model entry
sections.what: Describes a single mental model as a name and one line of explanation.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeping each model to a name and one line makes it easy to read at a glance in the brain picture.
sections.watch_out: The file sets no maximum length, so a very long line could overflow its space on screen.

sections.name: ModelFamily
sections.title: A group of related models
sections.what: Describes a family: an id, a heading label, which side of the brain it sits on (left or right), and its list of models.
sections.why: Likely reason: grouping the models lets the brain picture place each family on one side.
sections.watch_out: The side value must be exactly left or right, and the type check catches a typo only when the project is type-checked.

sections.name: modelFamilies (part 1)
sections.title: Left-side families: thinking, systems, maths and economics
sections.what: Lists the first left-side families: general thinking, systems, mathematics, and the first part of economics. Each model is one line, for example the map is not the territory or feedback loops.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code, beyond the header comment about the left side.
sections.watch_out: Each family's id is used by the brain file to group its models, so renaming an id breaks that grouping.

sections.name: modelFamilies (part 2)
sections.title: Economics, strategy, nature and art families
sections.what: Continues the economics list, then adds the military and strategy family on the left, and the physics, chemistry and biology family and the art family on the right.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Models are shown by name, so a duplicate name in the same family would appear twice with no warning.

sections.name: modelFamilies (part 3)
sections.title: Judgment and human nature family
sections.what: Finishes the art family with setting and performance, then holds the human nature and judgment family on the right, which lists biases and behaviours such as confirmation bias and survivorship bias.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The file does not check that each family has at least one model, so an empty family adds nothing to the brain without any error.

summary: Holds short one-line mental models grouped into families, which feed the hero brain picture, with logic families on the left and lens families on the right.
purpose: Supplies the mental model content that the brain picture shows.
why: The file's header comment says the lines were condensed from a reference article. Reason for the grouping beyond that is not stated in the code.
how: First, the shape of a model and of a family is defined. Then the families are listed in order, each with its side and its models, one line each.
inputs: Typed in by hand. The file reads no outside data.
outputs: An exported list of families, read by the brain file.
risks: The one-line wording is not limited in length and could overflow where it is shown. The source article named in the header is not in the project, so the wording cannot be checked against it.
debug: If a family is missing from the brain, check its side value and whether its id matches what the brain file expects. If a line looks wrong, compare it with the source named in the header comment, which is not in the project.
